job-applications.name: Job applications that sound like you and never lie
job-applications.creator: Joaquin Laria, from more than 20 real applications (Sep to Nov 2026)

steps.do: Read the whole posting before writing anything. If it contains any of the stop phrases, stop, write nothing, and tell the candidate which phrase you found.
stop_phrases: will not be providing visa sponsorship
unable to consider candidates that will require visa sponsorship
not eligible for any employment-based immigration sponsorship
must be authorized to work without sponsorship
steps.why: In the creator's first batch, 6 of 17 queued jobs were impossible on these rules. Reading first saves the work and keeps a rejection off the record.

steps.do: Find what the company sells, to whom and how it makes money, and write one real insight about why the business works.

Rewrite the resume for this posting: lead with the bullets that prove what it asks for, result first, in plain words. Use only facts and numbers the candidate confirmed. Readable beats keyword-matched. One page.
One page, 4 or 5 paragraphs. Open on a specific moment, not the job title. One paragraph on how the business works. Answer the obvious objection. Close with a direct ask.
Before submitting: one page each, every number confirmed, no dashes, none of the banned phrases, no mention of AI, work authorization answers exactly as the candidate gave them.
banned_phrases: i believe i would be a great fit

steps.do: Submit, then record the employer's confirmation word for word. A click is not a confirmation.

never: Invent a number, title, scope or result
Change a visa, sponsorship or citizenship answer
Apply to a job that bars sponsorship or requires citizenship
Mention AI anywhere in the application
